Package neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.subsea

Class UmbilicalFunctionalDesign

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.subsea.UmbilicalFunctionalDesign
public final class UmbilicalFunctionalDesign extends Object
Functional screening checks for a subsea umbilical: hydraulic response, chemical delivery, electrical drop, optical budget, weight ratio and J-tube pull-in.

All methods are pure static functions with the units given in the method name or JavaDoc. They complement UmbilicalMechanicalDesign (cross-section and armour design) with the functional checks that are normally documented in an umbilical design basis. Results are screening estimates and do not replace detailed design.

Version:
1.0

    • frictionFactor

      public static double frictionFactor(double reynolds, double relativeRoughness)
      Calculates the Darcy friction factor. Laminar flow (Re below 2300) uses 64/Re; otherwise the explicit Churchill (1977) correlation, which is valid for all regimes, is used.
      Parameters:
      reynolds - Reynolds number (dimensionless)
      relativeRoughness - relative roughness, roughness divided by inner diameter (dimensionless)
      Returns:
      Darcy friction factor (dimensionless)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the Reynolds number is not positive

    • hydraulicTimeConstantSeconds

      public static double hydraulicTimeConstantSeconds(double innerDiameterMm, double lengthM, double viscosityPas, double bulkModulusPa)
      Calculates the hydraulic time constant of a distributed laminar line, tau = R C / pi^2 with R the Hagen-Poiseuille resistance and C = V/K the fluid compliance. This is the constant of a line whose far end is held at pressure; a line closed at the far end (pressure step into a sealed volume) is four times slower, which is what UmbilicalHydraulicsCalculator.stepResponse(neqsim.process.equipment.subsea.UmbilicalFluid, double, double, double, double, double, double) returns (and it adds the compliance of the tube wall).
      Parameters:
      innerDiameterMm - inner diameter in mm
      lengthM - tube length in m
      viscosityPas - dynamic viscosity in Pa s
      bulkModulusPa - fluid bulk modulus in Pa
      Returns:
      time constant in seconds

    • actuationTimeSeconds

      public static double actuationTimeSeconds(double innerDiameterMm, double lengthM, double viscosityPas, double bulkModulusPa, double actuatorVolumeLitres, double supplyBar, double requiredBar)
      Screening estimate of the response time of a hydraulic valve actuator at the far end of a line: t = V_act/Q + tau, where Q = (supply - required)/R is the laminar flow driven by the excess pressure.
      Parameters:
      innerDiameterMm - inner diameter in mm
      lengthM - tube length in m
      viscosityPas - dynamic viscosity in Pa s
      bulkModulusPa - fluid bulk modulus in Pa
      actuatorVolumeLitres - actuator volume to be displaced in litres
      supplyBar - supply pressure in bar
      requiredBar - pressure required to actuate in bar
      Returns:
      actuation time in seconds
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the supply pressure does not exceed the required pressure

    • electricalLine

      public static double[] electricalLine(double loopResistanceOhmPerKm, double capacitanceNfPerKm, double lengthKm, double loadPowerW, double supplyVoltageV, double frequencyHz)
      Screening estimate of a single-phase AC electrical line. Only the resistive drop is included; reactance, skin and proximity effects are neglected. The load current is a first estimate P/V at the supply voltage.
      Parameters:
      loopResistanceOhmPerKm - loop (go and return) resistance in ohm/km
      capacitanceNfPerKm - capacitance in nF/km
      lengthKm - line length in km
      loadPowerW - load power in W
      supplyVoltageV - supply voltage in V
      frequencyHz - supply frequency in Hz
      Returns:
      array {loadCurrentA, chargingCurrentA, totalCurrentA, voltageDropV, receivedVoltageV}

    • weightRatio

      public static double weightRatio(double dryFilledWeightNPerM, double outerDiameterMm, double seawaterDensityKgM3)
      Calculates the weight ratio of a fluid-filled umbilical: weight in air divided by the weight of displaced seawater. Specifications commonly require a minimum ratio (for example 1.5); the limit is applied by the caller.

      outerDiameterMm - outer diameter in mm
      seawaterDensityKgM3 - seawater density in kg/m3
      Returns:

      Calculates the pull-in tension at the termination head for a J-tube installation, stage by stage: seabed drag, straight inlet section rising at an angle, bend to vertical (capstan effect) and vertical section, then head weight and contingency.

      Returns:
